title: Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv's Dnipro Bridges as Ukraine Strikes the Kerch Bridge Twice, Senate Republicans Unveil a $1.1T Defense Bill, and Five EU States Plan Rwanda Return Hubs
subhead: Russian missiles struck two major bridges across the Dnipro River in Kyiv and knocked out heating and water hours after Ukrainian drones hit the Kerch Bridge to Crimea twice in 24 hours; US Senate Republicans unveiled a nearly $1.1 trillion FY2027 defense appropriations bill as President Trump floated Kim Jong Un joining Thursday's Shenzhen summit; and five European Union countries announced plans for migrant return centers in Rwanda.

sections.heading: Russian Strikes Hit Kyiv's Dnipro Bridges as Ukraine Strikes the Kerch Bridge Twice in 24 Hours
sections.body:
France 24, DW, and The Independent — Russian missile and drone strikes hit two major bridges spanning the Dnipro River in Kyiv late Monday, damaging critical municipal infrastructure and knocking out heating and running water across parts of the Ukrainian capital as winter temperatures set in, Kyiv's mayor announced. The Russian bombardment came hours after Ukrainian long-range attack drones struck the 19-kilometer Kerch Strait Bridge connecting occupied Crimea to mainland Russia for a second time in less than 24 hours, damaging a road arch and leaving up to 2,000 vehicles backed up in queues (The Independent, The War Zone).

In Brussels, European Union foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas warned that escalating strikes across the Black Sea region are threatening vital commercial shipping, energy, and digital connectivity corridors linking Europe with the South Caucasus and Central Asia (Anadolu Agency). Meanwhile, EU foreign ministers approved new sanctions targeting 12 individuals and 101 entities accused of financing Moscow's war effort and supporting Russia's shadow oil tanker fleet.
sections.whyItMatters: Mutual strikes on the Kerch Bridge and Kyiv's Dnipro River crossings show both Moscow and Kyiv escalating attacks on transport and winter heating lifelines ahead of Thursday's Shenzhen summit.

sections.heading: Senate Republicans Unveil a $1.1T Defense Bill as Trump Suggests Kim Jong Un May Join the Shenzhen Summit
sections.body:
The Hill, Breaking Defense, and AP News — United States Senate Republicans unveiled a nearly $1.1 trillion defense appropriations bill for fiscal year 2027 on Monday, folding roughly $69 billion in weapons and shipbuilding priorities originally sought by the White House through budget reconciliation directly into the Pentagon's base spending bill. The legislative rollout coincided with the start of President Donald Trump's Asia trip—after extreme weather briefly forced Air Force One to reroute—beginning with Quad talks in Manila ahead of Thursday's trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen (Reuters, The Hill).

Speaking en route to Asia, Trump told reporters that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un could potentially join him, Xi, and Putin for an expanded summit covering nuclear weapons, regional wars, and artificial intelligence (The Independent, AP News). North Korean state media reported Tuesday that Kim inspected the Samjiyon mountain tourism zone near the Chinese border amid intense speculation over a possible cross-border trip to China (CNA), while Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Moscow with North Korean Workers' Party Central Committee Secretary Jo Yong Won.
sections.whyItMatters: Folding $69 billion of reconciliation defense funds into a $1.1 trillion base bill sets up a major congressional spending fight just as Trump floats adding Kim Jong Un to the Shenzhen summit.

sections.heading: Iran Rules Out UN Nuclear Inspections Until the War Ends as Vance Vows No 'Forever War'
sections.body:
CBS News, Anadolu Agency, and Al Jazeera — Iranian officials announced that Tehran will not allow International Atomic Energy Agency inspectors to access Iranian nuclear facilities damaged by US and Israeli airstrikes until the ongoing war formally ends (CBS News). In Washington, US Vice President JD Vance vowed that President Trump will not allow the conflict with Iran to become another 'forever war' even as US Central Command confirmed the arrival of a third American aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, in the Middle East (Anadolu Agency, South China Morning Post).

On the ground in Yemen, the internationally recognized government's military reported conducting 661 combat operations that killed or wounded 173 Houthi fighters as government troops repositioned from the Bab al-Mandab Strait to defend the southern port of Aden (Al Jazeera). Elsewhere in the region, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency reported a new attack on a commercial tanker seven nautical miles north of Oman's Khasab in the Strait of Hormuz, while Syrian and Palestinian officials reported that 23 Israeli military vehicles raided the southern Syrian village of Maariya and that an Israeli settler vehicle rammed eight Palestinians in the occupied West Bank (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Tehran's refusal to permit UN nuclear inspections until hostilities cease leaves international monitors blind to the status of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile.

sections.heading: Washington Curbs Remote Access to Nvidia AI Chips as Nasdaq Sinks 2.7% and US Banks Hit Outages
sections.body:
The Register, Financial Times, and South China Morning Post — The Trump administration expanded semiconductor export restrictions to additional Asian countries and imposed new 'Know Your Customer's Workload' rules barring cloud providers in Asia and Brazil from granting Chinese entities remote access to advanced Nvidia AI chips, moving to close the cloud-rental loophole at the center of the Megaspeed scandal (The Register, Bloomberg). Singapore confirmed it is seeking urgent talks with Washington to preserve 'trusted access' to US AI chips for local firms, even as Singapore's October non-oil domestic exports surged 79.8 percent on pharmaceuticals and marine structures (South China Morning Post, CNA).

In financial markets, the Nasdaq 100 sank 2.7 percent on Monday as Nvidia shares dropped another 4.1 percent ahead of Tuesday's third-quarter earnings release and the upcoming Anthropic initial public offering, with Nvidia's board dismissing the 'Bring Jensen Back' petition despite public backing from President Trump and Vice President Vance (Financial Times, BBC, CNBC). Compounding US infrastructure jitters after last week's Microsoft and FAA outages, major American banks including JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo worked to resolve technical glitches that temporarily disrupted customer online banking access (Bloomberg, BBC, The Independent).
sections.whyItMatters: Extending US export controls from physical GPU shipments to remote cloud workloads across Asia directly reshapes how global data-center operators lease AI compute.

sections.heading: Five EU States Announce Rwanda Migrant Return Hubs as Rio Tinto Pays $250M Over the Panguna Mine
sections.body:
The Guardian, BBC, and Al Jazeera — Five European Union member states—Germany, Austria, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Greece—formally announced plans to establish joint offshore immigration 'return centers' in Rwanda to process and deport asylum seekers whose applications have been rejected in Europe, a proposal welcomed by the European Commission despite legal and human-rights criticism. In Ireland, a Dublin court sentenced Riad Bouchaker to life imprisonment for the November 2023 knife attack on three children and a care worker outside a Dublin school that had sparked anti-immigrant riots (Al Jazeera, BBC).

In the Asia-Pacific and Latin America, Anglo-Australian mining giant Rio Tinto agreed to pay $250 million to begin remediating decades of environmental devastation caused by the abandoned Panguna copper and gold mine in Bougainville, Papua New Guinea (The Guardian), while Australian department store chain David Jones entered administration with more than $400 million in total debt (The Guardian). In Paraguay, authorities transferred ousted former President Santiago Peña—jailed on corruption charges following the collapse of Ueno Bank—to a military prison after reports emerged that he had been enjoying a private suite and gym in police custody (Al Jazeera, AP News).
sections.whyItMatters: The five-nation European pact to build deportation hubs in Rwanda signals a hardening shift toward externalized asylum enforcement inside the European Union.

bottomLine: As President Trump begins his Asia trip in Manila ahead of Thursday's Shenzhen summit with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin—and floats adding North Korea's Kim Jong Un—every major theater is seeing last-minute positioning: Russia and Ukraine traded heavy strikes on Kyiv's Dnipro bridges and the Kerch Strait Bridge, Iran barred UN nuclear inspectors until the war ends as Senate Republicans unveiled a $1.1 trillion defense bill, and Washington moved to block Chinese remote cloud access to Nvidia AI chips across Asia.
